note: Majority: American Samoa Code Annotated § 40.0401 (1962, PL 1-21; amended 1979, PL 16-53 § 22), as the American Samoa Bar Association publishes the Code: the age of majority of males and females in American Samoa is eighteen; the Social Security Administration's own legal opinion (POMS PR 07215.003) reads it the same way. Emancipation and the marriage age aren't held. Work: the federal Fair Labor Standards Act reaches American Samoa: 29 U.S.C. § 203(c) makes 'State' include any Territory or possession of the United States, and § 203(l) makes it oppressive child labor to employ anyone under sixteen (save a parent's own child outside manufacturing, mining and hazardous work; fourteen and fifteen may work in limited jobs and hours under the Secretary's rules, not held). Performers: § 213(c)(3): the child-labor provisions don't apply to a child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures, theatre, radio or television, so free. The Code's Wages and Hours chapter (A.S.C.A. title 32, chapter 3, its section list read) has no child-labor rule of its own; no other territorial child-labor statute was found. Service: none; there is no draft. 50 U.S.C. § 3802 makes every male citizen, and every other male resident, between eighteen and twenty-six register with the Selective Service System, a duty the form doesn't hold; American Samoans are U.S. nationals, not citizens, and whether the duty reaches them in the territory wasn't settled.

sources.title: Social Security Administration, POMS PR 07215.003 American Samoa (legal opinion)
sources.said: In American Samoa, the age of majority is 18.

sources.title: GovInfo: 29 U.S.C. § 203, Definitions (Fair Labor Standards Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: "State" means any State of the United States or the District of Columbia or any Territory or possession of the United States. ... "Oppressive child labor" means a condition of employment under which (1) any employee under the age of sixteen years is employed by an employer

sources.title: GovInfo: 29 U.S.C. § 213, Exemptions (Fair Labor Standards Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: The provisions of section 212 of this title relating to child labor shall not apply to any child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures or theatrical productions, or in radio or television productions.

sources.title: GovInfo: 50 U.S.C. § 3802, Registration (Military Selective Service Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: it shall be the duty of every male citizen of the United States, and every other male person residing in the United States, who, on the day or days fixed for the first or any subsequent registration, is between the ages of eighteen and twenty-six, to present himself for and submit to registration
